description: Interactive step-based process walkthrough for Grade 7 Mathematics — Data Handling. Shows the arithmetic mean calculation for two cricket players with different numbers of matches. Layout: two player cards side by side (Shubman in blue, Yashasvi in green) with match scores displayed as chips. Phase-by-phase reveal: first shows raw data and totals, then highlights the unequal match count problem, then shows sum calculation with animated addition, then count with number badges, then the division with animated fraction bars, and finally the comparison with the surprising result highlighted. Each phase slides in from the right with subtle transition. Active phase has a glowing border. Completed phases show a checkmark. Indian cricket context with player name labels in Baloo 2 font. 5-colour palette: blue (#3b82f6), green (#22c55e), white background, dark grey text, light amber for highlights. Touch-friendly step navigation. Mobile-responsive with cards stacking vertically on narrow screens.

teachingNotes.phase0: At Step 1 (given data), ask the student who they think performed better just from looking at the raw scores.
teachingNotes.phase1: At Step 2 (problem), emphasise the unfairness — Shubman had an extra innings.
teachingNotes.phase2: At Step 3 (sum), let the student try adding before revealing.
teachingNotes.phase3: At Step 4 (count), reinforce that different match counts make totals unfair.
teachingNotes.phase4: At Step 5 (divide), ask the student to predict who will have a higher average before showing the result.
teachingNotes.phase5: At Step 6 (compare), highlight the surprise: lower total but higher average!

instructionsForStudent: Watch as we solve this step by step. At each stage, think about what the numbers tell us. When you see the totals, ask yourself: is comparing totals fair when the number of matches is different? Then watch how dividing by the number of matches gives us a fairer picture.
